settings.nagLevelHint: Reminders go out as you set them. The level adds notifications in each mitzvah's critical time (the last third of the day, and up to midnight for the night mitzvot) and at the last time to start, with a minyan and alone, at least 10 minutes apart. Each mitzvah's screen can set a level of its own.

settings.quietHoursTaharahNote: Family purity reminders for the hefsek, the evening bedika, the onah bedika, the tevila and separation always go out on time; the morning bedika moves to the chosen time only when that is before midday.

accuracy.title: Important notice
accuracy.effort: We put a great deal of effort into making the times in the app as accurate as possible: they are calculated for your location by accepted methods, and the reminders are built from them.
accuracy.responsibility: Even so, we can make mistakes too: in a calculation, in the location data or in a reminder that did not arrive on time. Keeping each mitzvah in its time is your responsibility, and whenever in doubt, check a trusted luach and ask a rav.
accuracy.report: Found a mistake? We would be glad to hear about it: Settings → About and contact.

taharah.settings.title: Taharah settings
taharah.settings.rulesHint: Defaults follow the custom. Change a parameter only on a rav's instruction.
taharah.husband.hint: Husband mode: separation onot and mikveh night only, from the recorded onsets.
taharah.settings.lockHint: Requires fingerprint or face to open the taharah screens.
taharah.settings.deleteConfirmBody: Every entry is erased from this device. Settings stay. This cannot be undone.
taharah.settings.resetConfirmBody: All records, the minhag, the rules and the reminder times will be deleted and tracking switched off, as before it was turned on. You can turn it on again under Settings → Profile. This cannot be undone.
taharah.affects.preset: Choosing a minhag fills in every rule on this card. The rules decide the count, the separation onot, the calendar and the reminders.
taharah.affects.hefsekEarliestDay: The first day from the onset on which the hefsek tahara may be done. Affects the hefsek task and its reminder, and so the start of the seven clean days and the tevila night.
taharah.affects.mochDachuk: Affects only the notice in the hefsek form. It never blocks a record or changes the count.
taharah.affects.onahBeinonitDays: The day from the onset on which the onah beinonit falls: the 30th, or the 31st as well. Affects the separation onot, the calendar, their reminders and the onah beinonit bedika.
taharah.affects.onahBeinonitSpan: Separate only in the onah the sighting began in, or a whole night and day. Affects how long the onah beinonit separation lasts, on the calendar and in the reminders.
taharah.affects.ohrZarua: Adds a separation in the onah before every separation onah. Adds onot to the list, the calendar and the reminders.
taharah.affects.haflagaMethod: How the haflaga is counted: in days from sighting to sighting, or in onot from the hefsek (the Chabad custom). Affects only when the haflaga onah falls.
taharah.affects.role: Decides what is shown and what can be recorded. Woman: every record, bedika and task. Husband: only the separation onot and the tevila night.
taharah.affects.reminders: These settings affect only the notifications and the lock, never the count or the separation onot.
taharah.affects.deleteData: Deletes every record and starts the count again. The minhag and the settings stay, and tracking stays on.
taharah.affects.reset: Deletes every record and setting of family purity tracking and switches it off, as before it was turned on. Nothing else in the app changes.
